4. The Evolutionary Arms Race
The 20th century’s "miracle" has become the 21st century’s nightmare, as bacteria have learned to breathe through the very fire we used to kill them. Strains like carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae now stand immune to our "last resort" interventions, threatening to turn a routine scrape or a standard childbirth back into a lethal gamble. This rapid adaptation has outpaced our pharmaceutical innovation, leaving us on the brink of a pre-Listerian reality. What is the common term for these multi-drug resistant bacterial strains?

5. The Triassic Achilles Heel
Paleontological evidence from 240 million years ago reveals a creature whose greatest evolutionary asset was also its fatal flaw. Fossils of Tanystropheus have been found where the body is missing, but the skull and neck remain, severed by a single, clean bite at a specific vertebral weak point. This suggests a predator that understood the physics of decapitation and targeted the most fragile part of its prey's anatomy. What specific anatomical feature represented this marine reptile's "vulnerability by design"?
